name: truewind
description: Physics-first browser sailing simulator: rigging-shaped sails, foils, hull resistance, waves, real OpenStreetMap coastlines, live wind, AI racing.

paragraphs: A browser sailing simulator where the boat is not animated — it is computed. Every frame, the sails are simulated as cloth, shaped by the wind and by the strings you pull, and the air over their live shape is solved as one vortex lattice; that, the lift of the keel and rudder, the resistance of the hull, the heel, the waves and the tide are solved as forces and moments on a rigid body, 120 times a second.
It runs in any modern browser with WebGL, with no install and no build step.
The menu groups them (dinghies and skiffs, keelboats, multihulls, cruisers, classics) under tabs, with a search box; the chosen boat's specifications and description show below the list.
features: Sail sections are semi-empirical. The lattice is potential flow; each section's viscous lift and drag come from a fitted 2-D polar (depth, draft and ORC's drag), not from CFD. Whether a strip has stalled is decided on…

The cloth meets the rig as wires. The mast, the stays and the shrouds are lines the cloth's edges cannot cross (the main lies on the leeward shrouds running, a jib wraps the mast in a tack, the kite the forestay); a…

The boat under the sails is a mirror. The hull and deck sealing the feet is modelled as a mirror plane per sail, not as a body; the boom's gap above the deck counts as closed while it lies over the boat, as ORC's…

Heavy air. The automatic crew depowers by heel and by bow-down pitch (sheets eased, kite not hauled in, vang off, tack line down), and the VPP starts a boat in a breeze already under way with sheets eased, so in 25 kn…

The cloth's lines are stiff springs. The vang and mainsheet take their tackles' stretch, but a snatched boom still reads brief peaks no rope would carry (a rigid kicker 70+ kN for a step in a gybe); only with the boom…
